findings.text: 12 chemotype(s); the largest holds 6 of 25 molecules -- a series of several scaffolds has no common frame, and an alignment will invent one
the common framework (framework of the largest chemotype) has 34 heavy atoms, about 162% of a typical molecule, and 24% of the set can be cut at it
the 34 shared framework atoms sit 11.3 A apart between molecules, over the best of their matches (6 of 25 carry them) -- the molecules are not in a common frame
the chosen attenuation 0.1 is at the bottom of the grid: the search needed a value it was not offered, so widen it before believing the model

the descriptor baseline reproduces the activity almost exactly (q2 +0.984); on a set this size that is not chemistry but the measurement itself, reached through the file's own columns -- the nearest are mwila_hcl_adj (r 0.71), mw (r 0.67), calc:mw (r 0.67), mwila_pooled_adj (r 0.66). No descriptor conclusion can be drawn until they are excluded.
dropped from the descriptor baseline because they reproduce the activity rather than describe the molecule: mwila_pooled_raw -- if one of these is a real descriptor, name it and run again
the aligned model is +0.202 in q2 against counts (95% interval -0.400 to +1.096) -- the frame gains nothing over counts
the aligned model is -0.198 in q2 against invariant (95% interval -0.611 to +0.106) -- the frame gains nothing over invariant
the aligned model is -0.716 in q2 against descriptors (95% interval -1.260 to -0.451) -- descriptors alone do as well, so the geometry adds nothing on this set

why: the frame gains nothing over invariant, which needs no alignment to curate and cannot be done wrongly
